bullets.title: NVDA: JPM expects beat-and-raise with Q3 guide $107-108B; consensus $104B; 7th straight down day ahead of earnings
bullets.body: JPMorgan spec sales desk sees NVDA printing Q2 revenue ~$94-95B and guiding Q3 to $107-108B, well ahead of buyside bars and FactSet consensus of $104B. Sentiment has improved with material short covering; stock at 10-year valuation lows. NVDA has beaten revenue consensus for 20 consecutive quarters; options imply ~4.6-6.1% move. The stock entered Monday on its 7th consecutive down day despite strong supply chain signals. Separately, NVDA announced Groq 3 LPX in full production (3,400 tok/s), Vera Rubin NVL72 showing 30x throughput/MW and 35x lower token cost vs GB300, and strategic investment in Lancium (15+ GW AI factory pipeline).

bullets.title: NVDA price hikes to hyperscalers on memory cost surge; MU down 5.8%
bullets.body: Nvidia informed hyperscalers it will raise prices on AI systems shipped next year due to soaring memory chip costs. This triggered a sharp selloff in memory names, with Micron (MU) dropping 5.8% and SNDK falling 5.8% (Canadian-listed). Semiconductor sector fell 3.7% on the day vs. Nasdaq -0.76%. Some analysts view MU and SNDK as buyable at current levels, noting non-standard fiscal year ends and potential buyback eligibility.

bullets.title: MRVL: JPM sees AI custom ASIC business doubling to $4B in F28; GOOGL partnership worth $20B/yr; undervalued vs. NVDA/AVGO
bullets.body: JPMorgan's spec sales desk highlights MRVL as positioned for 15% sequential revenue growth (39% YoY) with a ~12% guide-up (50% YoY). The GOOGL custom ASIC partnership is described as 'transformational' at $20B p.a., but market is slow to credit this. MRVL trades at 35x F28 EPS vs. AVGO/NVDA in the teens, which JPM says reflects slow recognition of the GOOGL upside. Implied move is 8.8%.

bullets.title: ZG +3.2%: FTC settlement removes last major litigation overhang; Redfin partnership intact through mid-2030s; PT $48
bullets.body: KeyBanc flags ZG's FTC resolution as removing its last major outstanding legal case—Compass dropped March, RESPA dismissed July, Nashville MLS resolved earlier. The Redfin syndication partnership remains intact through mid-2030s, with exclusivity provisions removed and standalone advertising launching in FY27. ZG reaffirmed full-year guidance including 30% Rentals revenue growth in 2026E. Stock trades at 7.9x 2028E EV/EBITDA vs. 3-year median of 21.1x; KeyBanc PT $48 at 10x 2028E EBITDA.

bullets.title: PAYC: JPM raises PT to $264; 2Q revenue +10% YoY, margin expands 320bps; AI driving $130M+ in savings
bullets.body: JPMorgan raises PAYC price target to $264 (Dec-27) following a strong Q2: revenue $531M beat consensus of $513M, recurring revenue growth accelerated to +11% YoY, and EBITDA margin expanded 320bps YoY to 44.2%. FY26 EBITDA margin guidance raised to ~46% midpoint from prior 44%. AI self-hosting expected to generate ~$100M R&D savings plus $30M+ from third-party fees. JPM maintains Neutral citing 13x uFCF trading multiple already in line with peers.

bullets.title: DIS +2.6% on early executive retirement packages; enters bull market up 20% in past month
bullets.body: Disney offered longtime executives early retirement packages as a cost-cutting measure, driving shares up 2.6% on the day. Multiple sources characterize the move as part of ongoing efficiency initiatives. One analyst notes DIS is up 20% over the past month, entering what they characterize as bull market territory.

bullets.title: NFLX exploring integration of third-party streamers (Peacock, Fox One) into its platform
bullets.body: Netflix held preliminary discussions about integrating competing streaming services including Peacock (CMCSA) and Fox One (FOXA) directly into its app, per NYT/Bloomberg sources. Executives were involved in discussions; no deal announced. ESPN also announced a subscription price increase to $31.99/month starting September 17.

bullets.title: CRM: F2Q27 earnings 26-Aug; Agentforce monetization and F2H acceleration are key watch items
bullets.body: Street expects F2Q27 revenue of $11.33B (slightly above $11.31B guidance midpoint) and EPS of $3.27. F3Q27 consensus is $11.41B. Investors are focused on Agentforce adoption, pricing, and monetization details as well as any changes to F2H27 acceleration cadence and cRPO growth.

bullets.title: CRWD: Q2 earnings 8/26; consensus $1.44B revenue, $5.79B ARR; options imply 9% move
bullets.body: CrowdStrike reports Wednesday after market close. Street consensus: Q2 revenue $1.44B, EPS $0.29, ARR $5.79B—all essentially in line with management's guidance midpoint. CRWD has beaten revenue consensus 19 of 20 quarters. Q3 consensus calls for $1.51B revenue and $6.12B ARR.

bullets.title: INTU FQ4 debrief 8/25: Mizuho expects 'reset to expectations' but maintains Outperform; cuts estimates and PT
bullets.body: Mizuho is hosting an investor debrief call Tuesday at 8:30pm ET following INTU's FQ4 report. The analyst preview is titled 'Anticipate Reset to Expectations, Clearing Event'—Mizuho maintains Outperform but is lowering estimates and price target. Key issues include AI investment impact on margins and guidance commentary.

bullets.title: TLN, VST initiated Outperform at Mizuho; AI/datacenter power demand the core thesis
bullets.body: Mizuho initiated Talen Energy (TLN) at Outperform with a $405 PT, citing tightening PJM power markets and capacity auction at ~$330/MW-day. Vistra (VST) also initiated Outperform with a $169 PT as the best-positioned merchant power platform to monetize AI and datacenter electricity demand. NNE signed a strategic framework with Tillman for 2+ GW nuclear capacity by mid-2030s.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: California AG cancels deal meeting, accuses PSKY of bad faith; deal faces complication
bullets.body: The California Attorney General cancelled a meeting with Paramount/Skydance (PSKY) leadership, accusing PSKY of acting in bad faith and leaking settlement discussions. WBD gained 0.5% on the regulatory overhang for PSKY. JPMorgan also initiated MAX and ROKU at Neutral, and MTCH at Neutral with a $43 PT.

bullets.title: LRCX: Citi hosting CEO investor meetings Boston/NYC next week; maintains Buy
bullets.body: Citi is organizing investor meetings in Boston and NYC with Lam Research CEO Timothy Archer and Senior Director of IR Kenji Morita. Citi maintains a Buy rating on LRCX. Materials include business overview, product portfolio, target model, recent results, and key management questions.

bullets.title: HIMS down 8%: Visa notified company of excessive credit card disputes on weight loss business
bullets.body: Visa notified Hims & Hers of excessive credit card disputes related to its weight loss products business, creating a regulatory/payments risk overhang. The company is facing an estimated ~$75K bill and potential broader payment processing complications.

bullets.title: BE: Nancy Pelosi files to purchase up to $12M in Bloom Energy shares and LEAP calls
bullets.body: Congressional disclosure shows Nancy Pelosi filed purchases of up to $12M in Bloom Energy (BE) stock plus up to $5M in LEAP call options expiring June 2027, and 10,000 shares of INTC plus $500K in INTC calls. Multiple analysts flagged the BE trade as a data center power / behind-the-meter AI infrastructure play with bipartisan political support.

bullets.title: TTD files automatic mixed shelf of indeterminate amount; stock near $13.27
bullets.body: The Trade Desk filed an S-3ASR automatic mixed shelf offering of indeterminate amount on August 24. The previous comparable shelf was filed in August 2023 at $74.67/share, highlighting the stock's dramatic decline since that period.

bullets.title: AVGO: Credit risk rising as bond traders increase risk measures on massive AI financing deals
bullets.body: Bond market participants are increasing credit risk measures on Broadcom (AVGO) as it backs a massive $60B AI infrastructure debt financing. While not a near-term equity concern, the growing leverage profile tied to hyperscale AI deals is drawing scrutiny from fixed income markets ahead of AVGO's earnings in September.

bullets.title: WDC down 21% in a week, -43% from June peak; memory bear market deepens
bullets.body: Western Digital fell 21% over the trailing week and is making new lows in a bear market that began mid-June, with a 43% drawdown from the peak. The selloff is tied to NVDA's announcement of price hikes on AI systems due to memory cost inflation, which raises demand uncertainty for the DRAM/NAND stack. WDC is still up 53% over the past 6 months.

bullets.title: ARM: AGI CPU with 136 Neoverse V3 cores expected to drive $2B demand in 2027-2028
bullets.body: ARM detailed its AGI CPU architecture at Hot Chips: dual chiplets with over 100B transistors and 136 Neoverse V3 cores targeting $2B in demand in 2027-2028. The architecture is specifically designed to compete in the AI server CPU market.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE/CRDO/CIEN: JPM buyside survey ahead of Sept earnings; AI server orders and backlog the key focus
bullets.body: JPMorgan is circulating a buyside survey on earnings expectations ahead of September prints: DELL reports Sept 3 (AI orders, backlog, F27 EPS guide), HPE reports Sept 2 (AI system orders/backlog), CRDO reports Sept 1 (F1Q27 and F2Q27 guidance), and CIEN reports Sept 3 (F3Q26 revenue, GM, F4Q26 outlook). Jefferies' semiconductor bus tour Sept 15-16 includes CRDO, MRVL, SNDK, ALAB, and others.
